The first paragraph of the scrolling pane holds enough text to wrap onto several lines, with commas, clauses, and a few more words, so that the content detection treats the pane as an article.

The second paragraph continues the text, again with commas, clauses, and enough words to fill several lines of the narrow pane.

The third paragraph adds more lines, so that the pane has to scroll while the reader moves down line by line with the arrow keys.

The fourth paragraph ends the article, after which the pane cannot scroll any further and the page has to bring the line into view.
